name: The Lantern Moth Fossil
period: Late Pliocene, about 3.1 million years ago
facts: Wingspan of 14 cm preserved in blue-grey clay
Scales on the wings kept a faint iridescent sheen
Donated by the Hartwell Quarry Society in 1962

name: Skeleton of the Marsh Stilt-Strider
facts: Stood 2.1 m tall on hollow, stilt-like legs
Flightless; probably waded for freshwater snails
Eleven of the twelve known skeletons were lost in a 1904 flood

name: Ember Amber with Beetle
facts: A copper-coloured beetle, 6 mm long, caught mid-stride
Shows a droplet of the tree resin that trapped it

name: Cast of the Glasswing Pterosaur Skull
period: Early Cretaceous, about 120 million years ago
facts: Skull is 38 cm long with a thin, translucent crest
The original is too fragile to display
Cast was made from a scan taken in 1998

name: Thornback Trilobite Slab
facts: Forty-one trilobites crowd one slab, all facing the same way
Suggests a mass moulting event or a sudden current

name: Moonfern Leaf Impression
facts: Frond is 22 cm long with crescent-shaped leaflets
Named for its pale, moon-like leaflets in raking light
First specimen catalogued by Dr. Ines Abernathy in 1931
